what_it_does: This paper describes a specialized processor that makes video look sharper (super-resolution) by exploiting how video compression actually works. Most video super-resolution treats each frame as a standalone image and tries to guess missing details from scratch. This processor instead recognizes that video is encoded by storing only the changes between frames and occasional full keyframes—like describing a movie as 'the character stayed still' rather than redrawing the entire scene. By reusing motion vectors (the direction each part of the image moved) and residuals (the difference between predicted and actual pixels) that are already embedded in compressed video, the processor does less work while producing better quality. It can process 4K ultra-high-definition video at 210 frames per second.
